title: P28 Session 1: Blender Character Rigging with Claude MCP
goal: Create a functional rig for a 3D character in Blender and create a simple animation using the rig within approximately one hour, with Claude assisting me during the workflow.

Step 1.step_action: I will import/open the character in Blender and inspect the model before starting the rig. I will check the transforms, orientation, mesh structure, and character proportions, and use Claude to help identify anything that should be corrected before rigging.

nodes.label: Inspect character mesh and setup before rigging
nodes.detail: Opens character2.blend (a high-poly female military character, combined mesh 'mesh_node') and visually inspects it in the viewport. Confirms the character is already in a correct T-pose and properly oriented before starting any rigging work.

nodes.label: Draft a rigging request prompt for Claude via ChatGPT
nodes.detail: Opens ChatGPT and sends a screenshot of the character with the message asking for a proper prompt to rig the character using Claude MCP. Uses ChatGPT as an intermediate prompt-writing tool rather than working directly with Claude yet.

nodes.label: Generate a structured Claude MCP rigging prompt
nodes.detail: ChatGPT (chat 'Write Blender Rig Prompt') produces a structured prompt specifying a simple, clean humanoid armature, preservation of appearance/proportions/T-pose, and a single centered armature suitable for game export. The participant copies this prompt for use with Claude.

nodes.label: Read and copy the ChatGPT-generated prompt
nodes.detail: The participant reads through the structured rigging prompt ChatGPT produced ('So here is the prompt ChatGPT gave me') and copies it to use with Claude.

Step 2.step_action: I will create an armature and position the main bones according to the character's body. I will use Claude for guidance on bone placement, hierarchy, symmetry, and Blender rigging tools if I encounter problems.

nodes.label: Initiate first Claude MCP auto-rig attempt
nodes.detail: Opens the Claude MCP panel embedded in the Blender sidebar (chat 'Rigging a humanoid female character for game export', Sonnet 4.6 Low) and pastes the ChatGPT-generated rigging prompt to begin the first automated rigging attempt on character2.blend.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: paste gpt's prompt into claude mcp

nodes.label: Analyze character and begin generating armature code
nodes.detail: Claude views the file, takes anatomical measurements via the Blender integration, and attempts screenshots that repeatedly error ('Tool result is too large'). Begins writing Python code to construct the armature in multiple passes.

nodes.label: Restart Claude MCP session after disconnect
nodes.detail: The MCP connection drops mid-generation. The participant reconnects and resends the rigging prompt to Claude to retry the automated rig from scratch.

nodes.label: Build, bind, and test the humanoid character rig
nodes.detail: Claude builds a full humanoid armature with a hierarchical bone structure, parents the character mesh to the armature using automatic weights, and tests the rig by rotating major joints to verify that the mesh deforms successfully.

nodes.label: Manually test rig in Pose Mode and discover failure
nodes.detail: Switches to Pose Mode and manually rotates bones to verify the rig. Finds that bones are disconnected and movement does not transfer to the mesh as Claude had reported.

nodes.label: Conclude first auto-rig attempt failed
nodes.detail: Determines that Claude's automated rig did not actually work despite its self-reported success, concluding 'Claude couldn't rig a character.'

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: conclude claude could not rig the character

nodes.label: Decide to build the armature manually instead
nodes.detail: Rather than retrying the automated approach immediately, decides to build a basic armature by hand and ask Claude only to fix specific issues afterward.

nodes.label: Manually create armature bone chain in Edit Mode
nodes.detail: Using Blender's Armature Edit Mode, adds bones by hand starting from the hip and extruding through spine, chest, neck, head, and one shoulder/arm/leg chain, renaming each bone individually via F2 (Bone.001-Bone.009).

nodes.label: Mirror hand-built bones to the opposite side
nodes.detail: Applies X-axis Symmetrize to mirror the manually created left-side bone chain onto the right side of the character.

nodes.label: Attempt automatic-weight parenting and hit an error
nodes.detail: Selects mesh and armature and tries Ctrl+P With Automatic Weights to bind the manually built armature to the mesh; the operation fails with an error.

nodes.label: Open a new Claude chat with a custom technical-artist skill
nodes.detail: Starts a new MCP chat ('Parenting armature to character rig') and loads a custom 'Blender AAA Technical Artist Skills' skill the participant wrote to make Claude act as a senior 3D rigging artist.

nodes.label: Diagnose parenting configuration error
nodes.detail: Claude identifies that parent_type was set to OBJECT instead of ARMATURE and runs Python code to correct the modifier setup on the manually built armature.

nodes.label: Observe unexpected deformation and abandon character2.blend
nodes.detail: Tests the fixed rig in Pose Mode per Claude's instructions, but the armature deforms unexpectedly. Concludes character2.blend's geometry may be too complex for a quick manual/automated approach.

nodes.label: Close character2.blend and switch to a second character file
nodes.detail: Abandons character2.blend and opens CR1.blend, a simpler stylized anime-style female character (also a combined mesh 'mesh_node'), intending an easier test case for rigging.

nodes.label: Resend the rigging prompt to Claude for the new character
nodes.detail: Takes a screenshot of the CR1 character and resends the same ChatGPT-generated rigging prompt to Claude within the existing 'Parenting armature to character rig' MCP chat.

nodes.label: Build, parent, and refine the humanoid character rig
nodes.detail: Claude creates a HumanoidArmature, parents it to the CR1 character mesh, and tests the resulting deformation. It confirms that the arms, legs, and knees respond to pose changes, identifies that the clavicle and shoulder bones are positioned too high, and continues refining the rig to correct the misalignment.

nodes.label: Test rig in Pose Mode and discover the mesh breaks
nodes.detail: Manually tests the CR1 rig in Pose Mode; the mesh deforms incorrectly and breaks completely, contradicting Claude's self-reported success.

nodes.label: Conclude both Claude MCP auto-rig attempts failed
nodes.detail: Summarizes that across both the character2.blend and CR1.blend attempts, Claude was unable to produce a working full auto-rig: 'In both first and second challenge, Claude couldn't create a full simple rig for us.'

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: find mesh breaks, conclude both auto-rig attempts failed

nodes.label: Remove Claude-created armature and start fresh manually
nodes.detail: Deletes the failed HumanoidArmature entirely from CR1.blend, deciding to build a deliberately simplified armature by hand rather than attempt another automated pass.

nodes.label: Manually build a one-sided simple armature
nodes.detail: In Edit Mode, hand-builds a simplified armature covering only one side of the character: neck, head, spine chain, one shoulder/clavicle/upper arm/forearm, and one hip/thigh/shin/foot chain, intentionally not professional-grade.

nodes.label: Request Claude mirror the bones to the other side
nodes.detail: Sends a screenshot to Claude via the MCP chat asking it to perform only one narrow task: mirror the hand-built left-side bones to the right side of the character ('i made armature myself, its just left side of character, mirror it to right side as well').

nodes.label: First mirror attempt fails to locate armature data
nodes.detail: Claude cannot find the correct custom bone data, initially referencing a stale 'HumanoidArmature' datablock instead of the participant's new hand-built armature, and asks for a clarifying screenshot.

nodes.label: Provide a clarifying screenshot of the current armature
nodes.detail: Supplies a second screenshot showing the actual current bone structure so Claude can correctly identify which armature and bones to mirror.

nodes.label: Successfully mirror bones into a bilaterally symmetric armature
nodes.detail: Claude mirrors Bone.012-014 (left arm) and Bone.015-018 (left leg) as exact X-axis mirrors, reporting that both arms and legs mirrored correctly and the spine chain remained centered. Offers to rename bones with .L/.R suffixes.

nodes.label: Inspect the mirrored armature
nodes.detail: The participant inspects the newly mirrored armature in the viewport, explaining that Claude completed the symmetry and mirrored the hand-built bones onto the other side.

Step 3.step_name: Bind and test the character rig
Step 3.step_action: I will connect the character mesh to the armature and test the rig by moving different parts of the character. If there are deformation or weight problems, I will use Claude to help identify possible solutions and then make the necessary corrections in Blender.

nodes.label: Parent mesh to the mirrored armature with automatic weights
nodes.detail: Selects both the mesh (mesh_node) and the newly mirrored, bilaterally symmetric armature, then uses Ctrl+P > Set Parent To > With Automatic Weights. The parenting succeeds without error this time.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: bind the mesh to claude's mirror armature

nodes.label: Test rig by posing arm bones in Pose Mode
nodes.detail: Switches to Pose Mode, selects an arm bone, and manually rotates it (roughly 28-40 degrees) to verify deformation. The mesh follows the bones cleanly and the character can be posed correctly.

nodes.label: Confirm successful rig and summarize the working approach
nodes.detail: Confirms 'So it did work' and reflects that success came from building the armature manually (one side) and using Claude only for the narrow symmetry/mirror task, not from a full Claude auto-rig.

Step 5.step_action: I will review the completed rig and animation and look for any obvious technical or visual problems. I will use Claude to help troubleshoot issues that I encounter and make final improvements within the available session time.

nodes.label: Request Claude analyze and optimize the completed rig
nodes.detail: After summarizing the session's mixed results, decides to attempt one more improvement: asking Claude to check and optimize the working manually-built rig via the Blender integration.

nodes.label: Diagnose and correct structural and deformation issues in the completed rig
nodes.detail: Claude analyzes the completed rig and identifies problems with bone rolls and hierarchy, then applies corrective changes through the Blender integration. During testing, it detects an existing pose, clears it to inspect the rest state, finds that the mesh is not properly connected to the armature and that the left elbow still bends incorrectly, and continues adjusting the rig before summarizing the problems it found and fixed.

nodes.label: Attempt to restore the original pose and confirm the rig is broken
nodes.detail: Tries to return the character to its earlier working pose but cannot recover it, concluding that Claude's optimization pass broke the previously-working rig within the remaining session time: 'It broke the rotation of the character this time.'

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: claude's opt pass broke the working rig
